A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MMed-RAG and provide readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices. Retained material can be matched reliably despite appendix expansion and removal of the original qualitative cases.

before.justification: v1 reports original medical VQA and report-generation experiments, component ablations, alignment analyses, and backbone-transfer results.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds external validation, environmental forecasting, additional model comparisons, and retriever analyses.

M1.justification: The original three-component system remains, but v2 adds substantive procedural extensions: rationale-guided retrieval denoising using Med42 teacher/student models in A.6.12, and adaptation to LITE through a time-series/text retriever in A.6.4. These are evaluated method variants, beyond testing the unchanged method on additional datasets.

E1.justification: Beyond the retained five medical datasets, v2 evaluates environmental temperature and river-flow prediction on CRW-Temp and CRW-Flow, and external ophthalmology/pathology data from PubMedVision. It also adds direct image-to-text retrieval evaluation, substantially broadening domain and task coverage.

E2.justification: Table 11 adds GPT-4o, Gemini-1.5, LLaVA-v1.6, Qwen-VL-Chat, and InternVL-2 to the retained comparison. Additional evaluated comparators include Quilt-LLaVA, RetinaVLM, and several CLIP-based retrievers in Tables 12, 18, and 20. The original main-table comparator sets remain.

E3.justification: New evaluations introduce few-shot prompting, forecasting with RMSE/MAE, and retrieval with Recall@1/5. Existing training settings and dataset counts remain unchanged. A.10 additionally specifies an OR-rate denominator based on incorrect samples, conflicting with the initially correct questions described in retained Section 3.3; the PDFs do not establish which calculation was used.

E4.justification: v2 extends the original individual preference-subset ablations to combinations, compares general and MoE retrievers, examines few-shot sensitivity, adds external validation, and measures alignment across more models. These address substantial additional diagnostic questions. The five qualitative cases in v1 Appendix C are removed.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental repetition or seed counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The additional tables continue reporting point estimates; their use of 'statistics' does not introduce uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Original scores in Tables 1–5 and 10 remain unchanged, while v2 adds extensive results and BLEU-1–4 breakdowns. New Table 13 reports CRW-Temp RMSE of 2.02 for LITE versus 1.74 with RAG-PT. New Table 16 includes mixed external-validation outcomes: ophthalmology ROUGE-L is 14.98 for MMed-RAG versus 20.05 for the baseline. The original qualitative case outputs disappear.

T1.justification: The preference-data definition gains noisy input x*, and Equation (4) changes rejected-response conditioning from x to x*. This is a limited mathematical revision to the objective. Section 4's definitions, assumptions, and theorem statements, together with the Appendix B proofs, remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same three-component contribution and alignment claims. The headline improvements remain 43.8% overall, 18.5% for VQA, and 69.1% for report generation. The additional appendix evidence does not substantially redefine these central claims.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive explanations of specialist-model limitations, general/MoE retriever failures, retraining costs for unseen modalities, and poor few-shot performance. A.9 clarifies that its nearly random synthetic images differ from realistic domain shifts. These additions materially expand the discussion of mechanisms and applicability boundaries beyond v1.

D1.justification: v2 newly identifies the existing evaluations as zero-shot and describes the LITE time-series retriever and Med42 70B/7B rationale-generation setup. Existing hyperparameters, hardware, training-time disclosures, dataset counts, and the code/data link remain unchanged. The reproducibility statement mainly points to existing information.

R1.justification: Section 6 adds targeted discussion of DPA-RAG and RAG-DDR. New appendix material cites specialist models, MoE retrieval, and rationale-based denoising, while some general vision references are removed. The central positioning relative to RULE and medical RAG remains intact.

P1.justification: The main narrative and section order remain largely unchanged. v2 adds ethics, reproducibility, and acknowledgement sections, organizes expanded appendix results into numbered subsections, and adds explanatory sections A.7–A.10. Author affiliations, publication headers, and some wording are updated; Appendix C is removed.

P2.justification: The appendix presentation changes substantially: Table 11 expands, and Tables 12–21 introduce multiple new comparison and analysis displays. v1's five case figures are removed, while v2 introduces a different Figure 5 showing noisy images. Main Figures 1–4 and the principal table structures are retained.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1, the external validation, broader comparisons, and targeted retriever and preference-data analyses strengthen support for generalization and design choices. The net gain is limited by reporting problems: A.6.6 calls combination 1+3 best although Table 15 favors 2+3, and A.10 introduces an OR denominator inconsistent with Section 3.3. Original headline results and the absence of uncertainty estimates remain unchanged.
